body: issue-shape-gives-judgment-issues-a-bug-lead: Evidence, re-verified: the clarity prompt at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/triage-issues/prompts/clarity.md:22-24 still says 'Find the cause', 'Write the title as the cause', and 'Write the lead: the cause, then the harm and who sees it'; its approved example (lines 33-49) is a defect-shaped issue. The shape rule in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md (the 'The shape.' bullet, about line 406) says the title 'names the cause ... never the harm alone' and the lead is 'the cause, then the harm'; only item 4 tells judgment issues apart ('one sentence naming what the ruling decides'). Both files are the project's own source (no Materialized stamp; the stamped copies under .claude/skills/ are true-up's output). Filed facts still hold. Mechanism: the clarity pass applies one cause-then-harm shape to every routed or ruled issue, so a judgment issue whose subject works today gets a title and lead that read as a bug, and nothing in the shape asks for the current state of the thing or the decision the owner makes. Corpus: decision:issues-read-cold-before-the-owner commits to the one shape: 'rewrites its title and problem in one shape ... The title names the cause. The problem leads with the cause and then the harm'. Either option changes that sentence, so this is a question, not a tooling-only fix; the corpus is silent on judgment issues having a shape of their own. Harm: no accept-list entry; this is a judgment issue about the project's own tooling. Options: A (filed) two shapes keyed by issue kind: judgment issue title names the decision, lead states the current state (what is built, what works, what a user sees), then the choice; defect issues keep cause then harm. Cost: the clarity pass must tell the kinds apart (category defect vs any other is already the record's field, so the test is mechanical), the decision's 'one shape' sentence changes, and the approved example needs a judgment-issue companion. B (filed) one shape, every lead opens with the current state. Cost: a defect lead grows a sentence, and a judgment title still names a cause. Missed option C: keep cause-then-harm for the lead but key the title alone by kind (decision name for judgment issues). Cost: smaller change that leaves the owner's 'buries the lede' complaint about the first paragraph standing. Edits for A or B: clarity.md steps 1-3 and its example, the shape bullet in artifact-definitions.md, and the decision's Choice paragraph; the shape is also restated in the cheatsheet's Defect issues section ('the cause first, then the harm') at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md, which a fix must sweep. Recommended: A, since the issue's own case shows a judgment issue's reader needs the current state first. Siblings: none open.

dashboard-skill-places-no-missing-build: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/dashboard:NO_BUILD_PAGE serves a stub ('No build present ... Run /ok') when build_dir() finds no .ok-planner/dashboard/index.html, and version_notes() prints 'no page build at .ok-planner/dashboard/; the page says to run /ok, and the data routes answer'. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/dashboard/SKILL.md places nothing and says it 'edits no file in the project' and runs only five commands. Placement lives only in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up: carried_build() copies the family's browser/dist and versioned() stamps {{OK_PLANNER_VERSION}}; ESTATE_FILES places scripts/dashboard-gitignore as .ok-planner/dashboard/.gitignore, whose content is '*', so the placed build is never committed and a fresh clone or worktree lacks it. The installed front door keeps several versions in the plugin cache (25.4.0, 26.0.0, 27.0.0, 28.0.0 on this machine), so the pinned version's carried build is usually on disk. Filed facts hold. Mechanism: the build is gitignored by design, and true-up is the only placing act, so any clone needs a full /ok (which updates plugins and can rewrite the vendored layer) just to see the page. Corpus: decision:pinned-build-placed-at-true-up: 'the family's true-up places it ... ignored by git rather than committed. The build a project serves is the one its last true-up placed, never one retrieved when the owner opens the page.' decision:dashboard-started-by-skill: the skill is 'a thin verb over the same program'. decision:vendored-skills promises 'cloning it yields the working skills with nothing installed' (skills only), while README.md:31 and docs/integration-contract.md:68 widen that to 'the working suite', which the dashboard page breaks after a clone. Every option changes a decision, so route question. Harm: no accept-list entry decides it (the stub tells the user what to do, so A3 does not hold); a product-intent choice. Options: A (filed) /dashboard, or the service itself, places the pinned version's carried build from the installed front door's cache when missing or mis-stamped, sharing true-up's placement routine; falls back to naming /ok when that version is not cached. Cost: pinned-build-placed-at-true-up names two placing acts and drops 'never one retrieved when the owner opens the page'; the skill gains a file write; the placement routine must move to a module both reach. B (filed) the service serves the pinned version's build straight from the installed front door's cache and nothing is placed; true-up stops placing. Cost: the page breaks whenever that version leaves the cache, and the decision's Choice is rewritten. C (filed) commit the placed build. Cost: the decision's rejected alternative, a churning generated artifact in every consumer repository. Missed option D: keep the decision and narrow the promise: README.md and docs/integration-contract.md say a clone needs a true-up to place the page, and /ok gains a light path that places only the build. Cost: the owner still runs a verb beyond /dashboard. Recommended: A, since the cache already holds the pinned build and pinning stays exact. Siblings: none open.
